items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Gene Ammons took Charlie Rouse's place... became the tenor saxophone player that lasted through the whole existence of the band... The other thing that they recorded was a thing called... featured the tenors of Gene Ammons and Dexter Gordon

ctx.x: So it got so that after the solo was over, and Charlie Parker is back in the section and the section is playing, Charlie Rouse would still be sitting there with his horn across his lap, looking at the mike where Charlie Parker had played, and we would be into another chorus, the sax section is playing and everything, and Billy would tell Charlie Rouse, he'd snap his fingers, "Come on, man! Come on! Come on!" And Charlie would come to himself, grab his horn, and start playing with the section. This went on for a…

So Billy came to me, and said "John, I'm sorry, but I'm going to have to let Charlie Rouse go, because he's not ready for this." "What's the matter?" "I don't know what it is, but he just can't keep his mind on what he's doing." Anyway, finally they sent and got Gene Ammons, or they alerted him... I think he joined us later -- I believe it was in Dayton, Ohio, that Gene Ammons joined us. Gene Ammons took Charlie Rouse's place.
